task: Predict EGFR mutation status in glioblastoma. Classes: wildtype vs. mutant. On H&E, relevant clues include cellularity, pleomorphism, infiltrative growth, microvascular proliferation, necrosis, and small-cell or more monomorphic high-grade patterns that can accompany EGFR-altered tumors.

classes.0: EGFR wildtype glioblastoma with high-grade astrocytic morphology lacking the more stereotyped small-cell or monomorphic appearance often linked to EGFR alteration.
classes.1: EGFR mutant glioblastoma showing densely cellular high-grade tumor, often with more monomorphic or small-cell morphology, brisk proliferation, necrosis, and microvascular proliferation.
